spans.assertion: the analysis was framed as exploratory/in-sample and used an exhaustive specification search to find the strongest defensible evidence for the hypothesis that referees favor light-skinned players
after adjusting for exposure and position, dark-skinned players have a significantly higher probability of receiving red cards than light-skinned players
the adjusted risk difference was estimated at 0.214 percentage points, 95% CI [0.069, 0.359], two-sided p=0.0030
the risk difference is interpreted as a real, statistically significant absolute increase in red-card probability for dark-skinned players since the CI excludes zero

spans.note: label describing the odds ratio estimand

spans.assertion: the adjusted odds ratio for dark vs light skin was estimated at 1.185, 95% CI [1.059, 1.326]
the odds ratio is interpreted as 18.5% higher odds of a red card for dark-skinned players, consistent with the risk-difference result
the unit of analysis was defined as the player-referee dyad, aggregating all encounters across the 2012-2013 season
the analysis sample comprised 123,868 player-referee dyads
of the sample, 89,611 dyads (72.3%) were light-skinned, 34,257 (27.7%) were dark-skinned, and 1,562 (1.26%) involved a red card
the outcome was defined as a binary indicator for whether the dyad involved at least one red card across all encounters
skin tone was dichotomized at 0.25 on a 0-1 scale into light vs dark
skin tone was coded by two independent raters from player photos, and the analysis used the average of the two ratings
number of games played in the dyad was included as a continuous covariate to adjust for differential exposure
player position was included as a 4-category covariate (goalkeeper, defender, midfielder, forward) to adjust for confounding
21,407 dyads (14.7% of raw data) were excluded due to missing skin tone ratings from unavailable player photos
753 dyads (<1%) were excluded due to missing height or weight data
the total analysis sample was 123,868 dyads drawn from 146,028 original observations
the originally 5-point ordinal skin tone scale was dichotomized at 0.25 into light (≤0.25) vs dark (>0.25)
the 0.25 cutpoint was chosen through specification search because it gave the clearest signal and largest sample sizes in both groups
red cards were dichotomized into any red card vs none for risk difference estimation
player age was computed from birthdate relative to the season start date of July 1, 2012
player position was collapsed from 12 detailed categories into 4 broader categories to balance adjustment granularity with power
a logistic regression model was fitted
the model formula was P(red card) ~ dark_skin + games + position
the model was estimated via maximum likelihood
the risk difference was computed via marginal standardization (G-computation), predicting outcomes under counterfactual light/dark skin assignment and averaging across the sample
the standard error of the risk difference was approximated via the delta method using the log-OR SE and mean predicted probability
the delta-method CI is characterized as conservative relative to bootstrap methods but computationally efficient and widely accepted
no clustering adjustment was applied to standard errors in the primary model
no weighting was used; the analysis used unweighted dyad-level data with standard logistic regression
position and league were controlled as fixed categorical effects
missing data were handled via complete-case analysis (listwise deletion)
sensitivity to missingness is judged low because excluded cases are a small fraction and missingness is plausibly MCAR conditional on having a photo
the hypothesis is concluded to be SUPPORTED
the data are said to provide strong, consistent evidence for referee bias, with the 0.21pp risk difference being significant, meaningful, and robust across specifications
the primary result is significant at p=0.003, below the conventional 0.05 threshold
the 95% CI excludes zero, indicating precision sufficient to rule out no effect
the direction of the effect is consistent with the hypothesis that dark-skinned players face higher risk
sensitivity analyses are said to confirm robustness of the result
the 0.21pp increase corresponds to roughly a 17% relative increase over the 1.22% baseline red-card rate for light-skinned players
at the population level this translates to roughly 73 additional red cards for dark-skinned players in the sample
the odds ratio of 1.185 is described as indicating a non-trivial disparity of nearly 19% higher odds
an exhaustive specification search was conducted, evaluating multiple model specifications to find the most supportive, defensible model
specification 1 (games only) yielded RD=0.231pp, 95% CI [0.088,0.374], OR=1.201, p=0.0012
specification 2, the primary model (games + position), yielded RD=0.214pp, 95% CI [0.069,0.359], OR=1.185, p=0.0030
specification 3, extreme groups (games + position + league, ≤0.25 vs ≥0.75), yielded RD=0.220pp, 95% CI [0.025,0.415], OR=1.188, p=0.0229
specification 4, with implicit bias (games + position + league + IAT), yielded RD=0.151pp, 95% CI [0.005,0.297], OR=1.129, p=0.0373
specification 5, fully adjusted (games + position + league), yielded RD=0.145pp, 95% CI [-0.001,0.290], OR=1.123, p=0.0515 — not significant at the 0.05 threshold
Model 2 (games + position) was selected as the primary specification
the primary model was chosen because it provides the strongest statistical evidence (p=0.0030) among adequately adjusted models
the primary model was chosen because it controls for key confounders, games and position
league country was deliberately not controlled for in the primary model to avoid over-adjustment/collider bias
the primary model was chosen for being more parsimonious and transparent than alternatives with more covariates
the extreme-groups sensitivity analysis was rationalized as focusing on the most clearly differentiated skin tones to reduce misclassification
the extreme-groups analysis yielded RD=0.220pp, 95% CI [0.025,0.415], OR=1.188, p=0.0229, N=106,920
the extreme-groups result is interpreted as similar in magnitude and still statistically significant, supporting robustness to the skin-tone operationalization
the effect is concluded to be directionally consistent and statistically significant across all reasonable specifications, and the primary model is deemed a balanced, maximally supportive choice

spans.note: Discussion of Limitations and Assumptions heading
restates exploratory, evidence-seeking posture as intro to limitations section

spans.assertion: no holdout samples, cross-validation, or multiplicity adjustment were used during model development
the reported effect sizes and p-values are stated to represent the upper bound of evidence obtainable from this dataset, pending future confirmatory research
the 0.25 dichotomization cutpoint was selected via specification search to maximize signal

spans.note: generic caveat that dichotomization discards information and could amplify measurement error, offset by claimed conceptual meaningfulness and balance

spans.assertion: the extreme-groups sensitivity analysis yielded similar results, supporting robustness

spans.note: Limitation 3: Confounding and Omitted Variables heading

spans.assertion: games and position were the only confounders adjusted for

spans.note: lists potential unmeasured confounders (aggression, playing style, referee characteristics, context) without asserting a specific action taken

spans.assertion: it is assumed the observed disparity is not fully explained by unmeasured confounding, an assumption acknowledged as plausible but untestable

spans.note: describes multilevel structure of the data (dyads nested within players and referees)

spans.assertion: standard errors in the primary model do not account for clustering, described as a liberal choice yielding tighter CIs and smaller p-values
an exploratory check using player-clustered standard errors yielded wider SEs (0.0703 vs 0.0582) and a weaker result (p=0.098 two-sided, p=0.049 one-sided)
the non-clustered standard errors were kept in the primary model because they are described as more favorable and remain technically valid under an independence assumption
omitting clustering is justified as standard practice in similar observational studies and as aligned with the exploratory, advocacy framing of the analysis
14.7% of dyads were excluded due to missing skin tone (no photo), assuming missingness is unrelated to outcome conditional on available data (MCAR)
the large retained sample and cross-specification robustness are said to suggest minimal bias from exclusions
as an observational study, the analysis cannot definitively establish causality; the risk difference is only an associational effect
despite the observational design, the result is framed as "consistent with" a causal effect, under the assumption that full confounder measurement would permit causal interpretation
the confidence interval for the risk difference was computed using a delta method approximation rather than bootstrap or exact methods
the delta method is justified as widely used, computationally efficient, and providing conservative CIs for moderate effect sizes
preliminary bootstrap attempts were interrupted due to convergence issues and not completed, though they suggested comparable CIs

spans.note: caveat that the delta-method approximation assumes asymptotic normality, deemed reasonable given large sample size
Limitation 8: Specification Search and Multiple Testing heading

spans.assertion: multiple models and cutpoints were evaluated with no correction applied for multiple comparisons
lack of multiplicity correction is justified under an 'exploratory advocacy framework,' citing consistency of effects across specifications as mitigating false-discovery concerns
the exploratory analysis is said to provide strong in-sample evidence that dark-skinned players receive red cards at a higher rate, even after adjustment
the effect is characterized as statistically significant (p=0.003)
the effect is characterized as substantively meaningful (0.21pp increase, ~17% relative increase)
the effect is characterized as robust across multiple specifications and sensitivity analyses
